title: Steve Jobs 1994: Faith in people, objects, and why revolutions beat incremental gains
summary: In a 1994 Rolling Stone interview during his NeXT years, Jobs explains why revolutionary change needs technology, business and marketing aligned. He argues a new product must be 3-5x better to make people leave the mainstream, and that technology is only a tool while faith belongs in people.

principles.text: To get people to leave the mainstream, the reward must be 3-5x better, not marginally better.
principles.quote: What we learned was that the reward can’t be one and a half times better or twice as good. That’s not enough. The reward has to be like three or four or five times better to take the risk to jump out of the mainstream.

principles.text: Revolutionary change needs technology, business, marketing and a culture that matches why you built it with why people buy it.
principles.quote: To make step-function changes, revolutionary changes, it takes that combination of technical acumen and business and marketing — and a culture that can somehow match up the reason you developed your product and the reason people will want to buy it.

principles.text: Chase revolutionary change over incremental, even though it is harder and means being told you failed.
principles.quote: I have a great respect for incremental improvement, and I’ve done that sort of thing in my life, but I’ve always been attracted to the more revolutionary changes.

principles.text: Technology is just tools; the real faith is in people, who do wonderful things when given good tools.
principles.quote: Technology is nothing. What’s important is that you have a faith in people, that they’re basically good and smart, and if you give them tools, they’ll do wonderful things with them.

principles.text: Build great tools you believe in, then stand back and let them take on a life of their own.
principles.quote: I’m a tool builder. That’s how I think of myself. I want to build really good tools that I know in my gut and my heart will be valuable.

principles.text: Wealth isn't the goal; ultimately the goal is to seek enlightenment.
principles.quote: the goal is not to be the richest man in the cemetery.
